reason: Warm-condition signals reach the skin, where sweat glands can help release heat.
expectation: The signals will stimulate sweating, preparing heat loss through evaporation.

effect: The warm signal produced liquid sweat; evaporation remains to be demonstrated.
reaction: The distinction between sweating and evaporation is useful.
reason: Air at the skin provides the surroundings for sweat to evaporate.
expectation: Sweat will evaporate into the air, carrying heat away from the skin.

effect: Evaporation cools the body, with less evaporation in humid air; the warm goal is not yet marked complete.
reaction: The humidity comparison makes the distinction more concrete.
reason: Warm signals also reach skin vessels, which can help transfer heat to cooler air.
expectation: Skin vessels will widen, increasing blood flow near the surface and heat loss.

effect: Widening skin vessels completed the warm response by increasing heat transfer to cooler surroundings.
reaction: The heat-flow arrows clarify why increased skin circulation helps.
reason: Cold signals reach skin vessels, so I expect the opposite vascular response to conserve heat.
expectation: Skin vessels will narrow, reducing blood flow near the surface and heat loss.

effect: Narrowing skin vessels reduces heat loss without producing new heat; the cold goal remains open.
reaction: The distinction between conserving and producing heat is useful.
reason: Cold signals also reach skeletal motor pathways, suggesting a muscle response that produces heat.
expectation: The signals will cause shivering, increasing heat production through muscle activity.

effect: Shivering uses ATP to produce heat, complementing reduced heat loss from narrowed skin vessels; the cold goal is complete.
reaction: The contrast between producing and conserving heat is clear and satisfying.

mostWorthwhile.text: Comparing sweating with evaporation was most worthwhile: the planned humidity inset shows why liquid sweat alone does not guarantee the same cooling effect.

leastWorthwhile.text: The initial sweating result was somewhat predictable on its own; its value became clearer in the evaporation comparison.

surprise.text: The cold response distinguishes narrowing vessels, which conserves heat, from shivering, which produces it using ATP.

arbitrary.text: No action felt particularly arbitrary; the signals and target structures made the combinations purposeful.

continue.text: I would continue: comparing opposite responses and tracing heat flow made the constructions more interesting than simply assembling structures.
